Entity.Title: Institute for Educational Development, East Africa

Title: Upskilling teachers for effective academic writing
NewsSummary: Tanzania headteachers undergo refresher course on use of English to gain lifelong skills

content.text: Teachers in Tanzania face challenges in communicating in English since the language used in teaching and learning in public primary schools is Kiswahili. This affects their academic writing especially when they want to advance in their careers.

The Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (IED, EA) held a workshop for fifty primary school administrators in Bagamoyo, Dar es Salaam. The heads of school and deputies are enrolled in a two-year diploma programme in Education Management and Administration offered in collaboration with IED, EA under the Foundations for Learning project and Agency for the Development of Educational Management, ADEM.

"There are challenges in using English as a medium of communication in Tanzania. This workshop will build capacity for these head teachers not only to be able to communicate in English but also to write and make an analysis of an academic paper. The skills they will leave with from this workshop is lifelong" said Dr Mweru Mwingi, faculty at IED, EA.
The teachers were taken through the basic use of English in writing an academic paper through the three aspects of language which include reading, writing and listening.

Ms Shakila Mkwazu, an AKU alumna and professional development tutor at IED, EA emphasized that writing is not something that comes natural to many. Academic writing is technical and hence it is important that these teachers acquire the basic skills. Heads of schools are selected to hold prominent positions in the government and a skillset in writing comes in handy when preparing reports and documentation.

"This course is very good and will have a great impact in our careers as teachers and the communities we serve. Our leadership and teaching skills have been amplified after taking this course", said Onesmo Samuel, head teacher from Mnara primary school.

IED, EA plans to continue offering workshops and trainings in partnership with ADEM throughout the diploma programme. This will be done based on the academic term evaluation to identify the areas in the diploma programme that need more support.
